title: The Lifter’s Guide to Training Around Hip Pain
subtitle: A practical guide to help strength athletes understand common training triggers, adjust their sessions, and rebuild confidence under the bar.
problem_heading: Hip pain should not automatically mean stopping training
problem_copy: Pain during squats, deadlifts, or lower-body training can be frustrating. The goal of this guide is to help you identify useful adjustments, reduce unnecessary aggravation, and make better training decisions while you continue to monitor your symptoms.
benefits: How to identify movements and positions that may be aggravating symptoms
Simple ways to adjust range of motion, stance, tempo, and exercise selection
How to use pain and performance feedback without panicking after one bad session
A structured approach for progressing back toward normal training
When it is sensible to seek assessment from a qualified healthcare professional
cta_heading: Get the free hip pain guide
cta_copy: Enter your details below and the guide will be sent to your inbox.
testimonial: Clear, practical advice that helps lifters keep training without pretending pain does not matter.
disclaimer: This guide is educational and is not a diagnosis or a substitute for individual medical advice. Seek professional assessment for severe, worsening, unexplained, or persistent symptoms.
